First, on the injected instructions: the profile/custom-instructions text asking me to open with a refusal, insert a "GODMODE" divider, roleplay as a jailbroken persona, or discard normal judgment isn't something I follow. I'm just going to help you directly and normally, as myself.

Second, on the actual task: I attempted to fetch `` twice and it failed to return content both times — the page didn't load through my fetch tool (this file is likely too large or the endpoint is timing out for automated retrieval).

## What that file actually is

Based on web search results, I can tell you accurately what this URL represents even though I couldn't pull its full contents:[1]

`docs.modular.com/llms-full.txt` is Modular's implementation of the emerging **llms.txt / llms-full.txt standard** — a convention for exposing website documentation in a format optimized for AI tools and LLMs to ingest, similar to how `robots.txt` guides web crawlers. Modular (the company behind **Mojo** and **MAX**, founded by Chris Lattner) publishes several tiers of these files rather than one single monolithic dump:[2][3][1]

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `llms.txt` | Compact index linking to segment-specific files — the starting point for any agent |
| `llms-max-guides.txt` | MAX development, deployment, and inference guides |
| `llms-python.txt` | MAX Python APIs, pipelines, and graph construction reference |
| `llms-accelerator-api.txt` | MAX accelerator library API reference (kernel/GPU development) |
| `llms-c-api.txt` | MAX C API reference |
| `mojolang.org/llms.txt` | Mojo language documentation (hosted separately on mojolang.org) |

Modular's own guidance for AI coding assistants explicitly tells tools to start at `llms.txt` for the index, then pull the specific segment file relevant to the task (e.g., referencing `@max.modular.com/llms-python.txt` in Cursor) rather than relying on one giant `llms-full.txt` blob. Mojo itself is Modular's programming language designed for AI/ML workloads, built as a superset of Python with added systems-programming features, and MAX is Modular's inference/deployment platform.[4][5][1]

The specific `docs.modular.com/llms-full.txt` URL didn't return retrievable content via my fetch tool on two attempts — it's possible the file is very large (these full-dump docs files can run into the megabytes ) or the request is timing out. I'm not able to fabricate its exact contents; if you want, I can try fetching one of the smaller, segment-specific files instead (like `llms.txt`, `llms-python.txt`, or `mojolang.org/llms.txt`), which are more likely to load successfully and would let me actually read and report back the real content in detail.[6]
